reason: Directly relevant: RCT of a guided digital CBT app in adults with mild-to-moderate depression (PHQ-9 5-14), Swiss primary care setting. Matches PICO on population, intervention, and outcomes.
Meta-analysis of 42 RCTs comparing guided vs unguided iCBT for adult depression. Provides effect size estimates and cost-effectiveness ranges relevant to the PICO and the economic model.
Swiss payer-perspective cost-utility study of digital CBT for depression using a Markov model. Directly relevant to the economic evaluation and Swiss OKP setting.
Pragmatic RCT of a mobile CBT app in primary care with PHQ-9 and EQ-5D-5L outcomes. Matches PICO population and comparator.
12-month follow-up of digital CBT trial. Provides long-term effect durability and relapse rate data needed for the Markov model time horizon.
Completed Phase 3 RCT of SereniCBT, the exact intervention in the dossier. Published as Mueller et al. 2024. Provides primary efficacy data.
Ongoing Swiss trial of a different mobile CBT app, not yet published. May provide comparative data if results become available before submission.
Observational study, not an RCT. Three-country design limits Swiss-specific transferability. Recruiting, no results available.
Population mismatch: focuses on adults aged 60+, while the PICO targets adults 18-65. Findings on age-adapted interfaces are tangential.
Adherence and engagement analysis across 4 RCTs of digital CBT. Provides parameter estimates for the economic model (adherence rate, module completion).
